payload.name: spectral-band-entropy
payload.scope: A spectral feature that quantifies the uncertainty or information content of the normalized energy distribution within a frequency band, computed using Shannon entropy over the probability mass function of per-bin energies.

payload.body: For a frequency band with N energy bins having energies E₁, E₂, ..., Eₙ and total energy E_total = ΣEᵢ, the normalized probability mass function is pᵢ = Eᵢ / E_total. The spectral-band-entropy is H = -Σ pᵢ log₂(pᵢ), where the sum runs over all bins in the band with pᵢ > 0. H measures the uniformity of energy distribution: H = 0 when all energy concentrates in one bin, and H is maximized when energy is uniformly distributed across all bins. [formal: mathematics | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: For a frequency band defined by lower and upper bounds [f_low, f_high) and a spectral decomposition with N frequency bins indexed i=1..N, each with a complex amplitude A_i and frequency f_i where f_low <= f_i < f_high: the distribution is the ordered vector v = (|A_1|^2, |A_2|^2, ..., |A_N|^2), where |A_i|^2 is the energy of bin i. The parameters are the band bounds and the spectral decomposition method. The persistence mechanism is the explicit storage of the N-tuple of non-negative scalars ordered by bin index. [formal: the mathematical representation | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Removal test (Law 8b): does CF stop operating if the spectral-band-peak entry is removed? No. CF = max(E_i)/RMS(E_i) operates on the band's per-bin energy vector (the band-distribution); max(E_i) is a sub-computation inside CF's own formula, not an input supplied by the peak concept. The peak entry merely names that reduction — a sub-computation/numerator relationship, not an operational dependency (identity and sub-computation are not dependency, Law 8b). CF's true input is the distribution: a CF DERIVED_FROM/DEPENDS_ON band-distribution edge is the accurate one. This re-files a claim the court already struck on the same reasoning.
